lesson.subtitle: Lesson 19 -- From Data to Story: What You Have Found So Far
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Dejair Caitano do Nascimento | Lesson 19 -- From Data to Story
lesson.grammar_point: present perfect for results so far: have found, have tested, yet, so far

listenings.text: So what happened was this. Two years ago, we were testing a new pain drug in a cohort of sixty patients. Everything looked normal, but then a nurse noticed something unexpected. The patients who took the drug in the morning reported less pain than the patients who took it at night. At first, we thought it was a mistake in the data. So far, we have checked the data three times, and the pattern is still there. We have also measured the level of the drug in the blood, and it is the same in both groups. So the time of day might be a factor. It is a preliminary finding, but because of this, we have changed our protocol. If you are interested, I would be happy to share the numbers with you.

In our clinic, we had a big problem with treatment adherence. Many patients stopped their medicine after two or three months. For years, we thought the reason was the side effects. Then, last year, we started to call every patient once a month, just to ask how they were. We were not trying to change anything. We only wanted to collect data. But something shifted. Since we started the calls, adherence has gone up from fifty to almost eighty percent. We have not changed the drug, the dose or the doctors. The only new thing is the phone call. So far, it is the cheapest intervention we have ever tested.
